newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht steady late, interbank rate rises.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht steady late, interbank rate rises.

text.p: The Thai baht was steady following quiet afternoon trading on Friday with investors reluctant to take positions ahead of the four-day Thai New Year holiday period from Saturday, traders said.

"Nobody wanted to do anything ahead of the long weekend and it was so quiet it would have been hard to get out of positions during the afternoon if you wanted to," said a dealer at Thai Danu Bank Plc.
The baht was trading late at 26.60/26.80 per dollar, unchanged from earlier in the day. The one month swap premium was also unmoved at 7/8 satang/dollar.
Patterns of dollar/baht trade indicated growing foreign confidence in the currency despite recent surges in the dollar against the yen, traders said.

"Most investors are still bullish on the dollar as they believe US rates will rise ... but the situation is very good at the moment with the baht trading within the band and the forward swap at low levels," he said.
Cash demand ahead of the holiday period saw the interbank overnight offered rate rise to 9.50-10.00 percent from 8.50-9.00 percent earlier, dealers said.
